divisions.title: XVII. Foreigners in China—A Jewish Synagogue, etc.

summary: Simon Adler Stern, a Philadelphia businessman, went to China in 1887 for a friend, “W. B.” (the book is dedicated to Wharton Barker), to represent him in business matters. These are his letters home, lightly revised. He crossed the United States by rail in April, sailed from San Francisco to Yokohama, and spent some weeks in Yokohama and Tokio, going on by Kobé and Nagasaki to Shanghai and then by Cheefoo to Tientsin, before returning by Yokohama in August. He writes about hotels and restaurants, a Japanese dinner, a fire, street life, a Chinese theatre, the foreign residents and a synagogue at Shanghai, treaty revision in Japan, and the prospects for railways in China. An appendix reprints three newspaper pieces.
